author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest opened up about the difficulty of staying truthful while living inside a culture she described as deeply cynical, one that doesn't really like people and wants to reduce them to consumers. She explained how even innocuous online activity, like browsing Facebook Marketplace for secondhand furniture, ends up pushing a constant stream of negative and unsettling content into her feed. She described that exposure as a genuine contaminant, something that can quietly shift an entire family's mood from peaceful to unsettled without anyone even realizing why. Sometimes the hardest part of modern life isn't what you're looking for, it's what keeps finding you.

title: We all knew it...

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest argued that the British government has refused to release data on the relationship between vaccines and excess deaths, claiming the numbers would be damning enough to change public opinion overnight if they ever came out. He connected this reluctance to a broader pattern he sees across several major moments in recent history, arguing that officials rarely come clean voluntarily and instead tend to obscure or deny until the truth eventually surfaces on its own. He specifically pointed to financial ties between UK officials and the companies awarded pandemic contracts as one thread worth pulling on. Russell listened as his guest framed it as a race against time, trying to expose the machine before it does more damage.
